properties.title: OCPP Connection Failure (E217) on NX-400
properties.problemStatement: NX-400 dual-socket units running firmware 4.8 intermittently lose their OCPP 2.0.1 connection to the Polaris Charge Cloud backend, logging error E217, after roughly 72 hours of continuous uptime under high session volume.
properties.symptoms: The unit continues to charge locally and the display remains normal, but Polaris stops receiving heartbeat and status updates and cannot deliver remote start/stop/reset commands. No Ethernet link-down event accompanies the disconnect, ruling out a physical connectivity cause. The condition recurs roughly every 72 hours on affected dual-socket units unless the OCPP client is restarted or the unit is power-cycled.
properties.environment: NX-400, firmware 4.8 only; both AC sockets in active use; Ethernet or 4G backend link otherwise healthy.
properties.possibleCauses: Firmware 4.8's OCPP 2.0.1 session-resume improvements introduced a session-token cache leak in the OCPP client. The eviction logic that should reclaim expired entries is not correctly wired to the WebSocket keep-alive heartbeat, so entries accumulate until the client's memory pool is exhausted at roughly the 72-hour mark, at which point the WebSocket handler fails silently. Full root-cause detail is in KI-NX400-004.
properties.resolution: Until the unit is upgraded, configure a scheduled nightly OCPP reconnect job in Polaris Charge Cloud (Device Management module) that forces a WebSocket reconnect for each affected NX-400 unit during a low-traffic window (e.g. 03:00 local time). This resets the session-token cache before it approaches the 72-hour threshold and has fully prevented E217 in field trials. The permanent fix ships in firmware 4.8.1 (released 2025-03), which patches the cache eviction logic so expired entries are correctly reclaimed on each heartbeat; units upgraded to 4.8.1 show no recurrence beyond 30 days of continuous uptime. Prioritize the 4.8.1 upgrade and remove the nightly-reconnect job once it is confirmed installed. See KI-NX400-004 for the full root-cause writeup and REL-NX400-4.8.1 for the firmware release note.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the unit shows Online in Polaris Device Management with a current heartbeat timestamp. Confirm the scheduled reconnect job's last-run log shows a successful WebSocket reconnect. After upgrading to 4.8.1, monitor uptime past 72 hours and confirm no recurrence of E217.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate to engineering if E217 recurs on a unit already running firmware 4.8.1, or if the nightly reconnect job itself fails to reconnect.
properties.tags: OCPP, E217, NX-400, firmware, workaround

properties.title: Charger Offline / Heartbeat Lost (E101) on NX-100
properties.problemStatement: NX-100 units on Wi-Fi intermittently show as Offline in Polaris and log E101 after a Wi-Fi access point roaming event or a brief signal drop, even though the unit itself is powered and operating normally.
properties.symptoms: The local display continues to operate and any in-progress session is not interrupted, but Polaris marks the charger Offline and stops receiving heartbeat and status updates until the Wi-Fi link recovers, which can take several minutes without intervention.
properties.environment: NX-100 connected over Wi-Fi (not Ethernet); most frequent at sites with marginal signal strength or multiple access points.
properties.possibleCauses: The NX-100's Wi-Fi stack does not currently re-establish the OCPP heartbeat channel automatically after a roaming or signal-loss event. The underlying TCP session is torn down by the access point, but the OCPP client does not detect this until its own heartbeat timeout (default 300 seconds) expires, and does not always reconnect without an application-layer nudge. See KI-NX100-001 for the tracked defect.
properties.resolution: Where practical, connect the unit to Ethernet instead of Wi-Fi, which removes the roaming trigger entirely and is the primary recommendation for any site with an available network drop. For Wi-Fi-only installations, reduce the heartbeat interval from 300 seconds to 60 seconds in the unit's Polaris device configuration; this does not prevent the disconnect but shortens the visibility gap to under 2 minutes in field testing. No firmware fix has shipped yet.
properties.verificationSteps: Check the unit's status in Polaris Device Management and confirm heartbeat resumes within the configured interval. After switching to Ethernet, confirm no further E101 events over a 7-day observation window.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if E101 persists on a unit already migrated to Ethernet, which points to a different root cause.
properties.tags: E101, heartbeat, Wi-Fi, NX-100

properties.title: Charger Offline / Heartbeat Lost (E101) on NX-200
properties.problemStatement: An NX-200 unit shows as Offline in Polaris and logs E101, but the unit's own local display and any in-progress session appear unaffected.
properties.symptoms: Polaris stops receiving heartbeat and status updates and the unit cannot be reached for remote commands. Depending on the site's connectivity option, this can accompany an Ethernet link-down event, a Wi-Fi disconnect, or (on units with the optional 4G add-on) a cellular registration drop.
properties.environment: NX-200, any connectivity option (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, or optional 4G add-on module).
properties.possibleCauses: Most commonly an upstream network interruption (switch reboot, DHCP lease failure, ISP outage) rather than a unit-side fault. Less commonly, a stuck OCPP client session that fails to reconnect automatically after the link is restored.
properties.resolution: First confirm the site's network is actually up (ping the unit's IP, check the upstream switch/router). If the network is healthy but the unit still shows Offline, issue a remote reboot from Polaris Device Management; if the remote reboot itself fails, a local power cycle at the breaker resolves the stuck session in the large majority of cases. For sites with recurring E101 unrelated to a specific outage, review the connectivity option in use -- Ethernet is the most reliable and is recommended over Wi-Fi or 4G where a network drop is available.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the unit returns to Online in Polaris within a few minutes of the network being restored or the unit being power-cycled. Review the heartbeat history to confirm no further gaps.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if the unit remains Offline after a confirmed-healthy network and a full power cycle.
properties.tags: E101, heartbeat, NX-200, connectivity

properties.title: RFID Card Rejected (E117) on NX-200
properties.problemStatement: A driver's RFID card, confirmed valid and provisioned in Polaris, is rejected with E117 on an NX-200 unit, most often on the very first badge attempt of the day.
properties.symptoms: The reader shows a rejection rather than no response at all, and a second tap moments later typically succeeds. On early-production (hardware revision A) units, cold outdoor installations can instead show no read event at all rather than a logged rejection, especially below freezing.
properties.environment: NX-200, any firmware; symptom most pronounced after the unit has been idle overnight, or at cold-climate sites on hardware revision A.
properties.possibleCauses: On units with older RFID reader driver versions, the reader fails to fully re-initialize its antenna gain calibration after the unit's overnight low-power idle state, causing marginal reads to fail even though the card is valid (see KI-NX200-003). On hardware-revision-A units specifically, the antenna PCB trace layout is more sensitive to cold-temperature impedance drift, reducing effective read range (see KI-NX200-006). Less commonly, the card itself has been deactivated or reassigned in Polaris.
properties.resolution: First confirm the card is still active and correctly assigned in Polaris Driver Management. If confirmed valid, instruct the driver to tap a second time, which reliably succeeds since the reader recalibrates on the first failed read; disabling overnight low-power idle mode also removes the trigger at the cost of slightly higher standby power draw. Units that have received the RFID reader driver update no longer exhibit the idle-related rejection. On cold-climate hardware-revision-A units, instruct users to hold the card against the reader target for a full second and center it precisely; a field antenna-board replacement kit is available through support for sites with frequent complaints.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the card authenticates successfully on a second tap. After a driver update or antenna-board replacement, confirm zero first-tap-of-the-day rejections over a 2-week sample.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if a confirmed-valid, confirmed-provisioned card is rejected consistently across multiple attempts and multiple days.
properties.tags: E117, RFID, NX-200, idle mode, hardware revision A

properties.title: RFID Card Rejected (E117) on Nova DC (DX Series) Units
properties.problemStatement: A driver's RFID card is rejected with E117 on a Nova DC unit (DX-60/120/240/360), and the card is confirmed active in Polaris Driver Management.
properties.symptoms: The reader displays a clear rejection message rather than a blank/no-response state. The same card may succeed on a different DX unit at the same site, or after a short wait, which points away from the card itself as the cause.
properties.environment: Any Nova DC unit (DX-60, DX-120, DX-240, DX-360), any firmware version.
properties.possibleCauses: The most common causes are: the card was recently reassigned or deactivated in Polaris and the unit's local authorization cache has not yet refreshed; the unit has a temporarily degraded backend connection and is falling back to a stale local authorization list; or, rarely, physical damage/wear to the card itself.
properties.resolution: Confirm the card's status directly in Polaris Driver Management rather than relying on the unit's cached view. If the card is correctly provisioned, force a local authorization-cache refresh from Polaris Device Management (Refresh Local Authorization List action) and retry. If the unit's backend connection is degraded, resolve connectivity first (see the Ethernet/4G connectivity articles for this product) since authorization-list refreshes cannot complete while offline. Persistent rejection of a confirmed-good card on a fully connected unit warrants trying a spare loaner card to rule out physical card damage.
properties.verificationSteps: After a cache refresh, confirm the card authenticates successfully on the affected unit. Confirm the unit's connectivity status is Online at the time of the retry.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if the card is rejected after a confirmed cache refresh and confirmed healthy connectivity.
properties.tags: E117, RFID, DX series, authorization cache

properties.title: Vehicle Not Charging After Successful RFID Authentication (NX-200)
properties.problemStatement: An NX-200 session authenticates successfully (the RFID tap is accepted and the display shows a session starting) but the vehicle never actually draws current.
properties.symptoms: The unit's display and Polaris both show a session as Active, but the vehicle's own dashboard reports it is not charging, and the reported current draw in Polaris stays at or near zero for the duration of the session attempt.
properties.environment: NX-200, any firmware; occurs across a range of vehicle makes, ruling out a single-vehicle compatibility issue in most cases.
properties.possibleCauses: The vehicle's own onboard charger has not completed its handshake with the unit (common with some vehicles that require the cable to be fully seated and locked before proceeding); the vehicle's charge scheduling app has a delayed-start timer active that the driver was not aware of; or, less commonly, a fault on the unit's contactor prevents power delivery even though the session shows as authenticated.
properties.resolution: Confirm the connector is fully seated and the plug-lock indicator shows locked; a partially seated connector can pass authentication but fail the subsequent charging handshake. Ask the driver to check their vehicle's own app or in-cabin settings for an active delayed-start or scheduled-charging timer, which is a frequent, easily-missed cause. If both are ruled out, end the session, unplug and replug fully, and retry; a session that authenticates but never draws current on repeated attempts, across more than one vehicle, indicates a contactor fault requiring a technician visit.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm current draw appears in Polaris within 2 minutes of session start on a retry. If escalating for a suspected contactor fault, capture the unit's session log for the failed attempts.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate for an on-site technician visit if current draw stays at zero across repeated attempts with more than one vehicle and the connector is confirmed fully seated.
properties.tags: charging, contactor, plug lock, NX-200

properties.title: Vehicle Not Charging on Nova DC (DX-60) Fast Charger
properties.problemStatement: A CCS2 session on a DX-60 unit authenticates and the unit reports a session in progress, but the vehicle does not accept a charge or accepts a charge at effectively zero power.
properties.symptoms: The unit's display shows Charging, but the vehicle's dashboard reports no charging activity or an immediate charge-stopped state; some vehicles surface a generic "charging station communication error" message on their own display.
properties.environment: DX-60, any firmware; most often reported with vehicles performing their first DC fast-charge session on this specific unit.
properties.possibleCauses: A failed or incomplete CCS2 pre-charge/insulation-check handshake, most commonly caused by a vehicle-side battery management system that has not yet finished its own pre-conditioning; the vehicle's maximum accepted DC current being below the level the unit expects to negotiate, which some vehicle firmware versions handle poorly; or a temporary DC output fault on the unit itself.
properties.resolution: End the session cleanly from the unit (not by simply unplugging), wait 30 seconds, and retry; this clears a stuck handshake state in the large majority of cases. If the vehicle has an active pre-conditioning routine (common on cold-battery starts), advise the driver to wait a few minutes before retrying rather than repeatedly unplugging and replugging, which can restart the pre-conditioning timer. If the fault recurs on the same unit with multiple different vehicles, treat it as a unit-side DC output fault and dispatch a technician; if it only occurs with one specific vehicle model, log the model and firmware version for the compatibility tracking list.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the retry session shows nonzero current draw within the first minute of the charging phase. Record the vehicle make/model if the issue is vehicle-specific.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate for a technician visit if the fault reproduces across multiple vehicle models on the same unit.
properties.tags: DC fast charging, CCS2, handshake, DX-60

properties.title: Charging Session Unexpectedly Stops Mid-Session (NX-400 / NX-450)
properties.problemStatement: A charging session on an NX-400 or NX-450 unit ends on its own before the vehicle is full or the driver stops it, with no user action taken.
properties.symptoms: The unit's display returns to idle/ready and Polaris logs the session as ended, without a corresponding driver-initiated stop event. On dual-socket units, the interruption sometimes coincides with a second session starting or stopping on the paired socket.
properties.environment: NX-400 or NX-450, dual-socket configuration most commonly affected.
properties.possibleCauses: A dynamic load-balancing reallocation event that briefly drops the socket's current budget to zero rather than smoothly ramping it down (see the load-balancing article for this product); an OCPP-level remote stop command issued unintentionally from Polaris; a circuit-protection trip on the site's own upstream breaker unrelated to the unit; or a vehicle-side stop condition (battery full, thermal limit reached, user app command).
properties.resolution: Check the unit's session log and the Polaris event history for the exact stop reason -- this is always recorded even when not surfaced on the local display, and distinguishes a load-balancing event, a remote command, a breaker trip, or a vehicle-initiated stop. For a load-balancing-related stop, review the site's load-balancing configuration polling interval; for a suspected unintended remote stop, audit recent Polaris user activity for the site. If the session log shows the unit's own breaker tripped, follow the circuit breaker trip article for this product rather than treating it as a session-management issue.
properties.verificationSteps: Retrieve the session's stop-reason code from the Polaris event history and confirm it matches one of the causes above before closing the ticket.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if the session log shows no recorded stop reason at all, which indicates a logging or firmware defect rather than an expected trigger.
properties.tags: session stop, load balancing, NX-400, NX-450

properties.title: Charging Session Unexpectedly Stops on DX-240 / DX-360 Logistics Hub Installations
properties.problemStatement: A DC fast-charge session on a modular DX-240 or DX-360 unit stops before completion, most often observed at logistics-hub sites running multiple simultaneous sessions across the unit's modular power stages.
properties.symptoms: The gun in use shows Ready/idle rather than Charging, and Polaris logs a session-ended event; other guns on the same modular unit may or may not be affected simultaneously depending on which power stage was reallocated.
properties.environment: DX-240 (2x120kW) or DX-360 (3x120kW) modular unit; most commonly reported at sites operating near the unit's total rated capacity with several guns active.
properties.possibleCauses: A modular power-stage reallocation, where the unit's internal power-sharing logic shifts a stage from one gun to another to satisfy a higher-priority or longer-running session, briefly interrupting the lower-priority session rather than gracefully ramping it; an overcurrent protection trip on an undersized upstream supply (see the circuit breaker trip article for this product); or a vehicle-initiated stop.
properties.resolution: Review the gun's session log for the stop reason. A power-stage reallocation event is expected behavior under heavy simultaneous demand and is not a defect; sites that frequently hit this condition should review whether the installed unit's total rated power (240kW or 360kW) is adequately sized for typical simultaneous-session demand at that hub, since the unit shares its modular stages across active guns rather than guaranteeing full power to every gun at once. If the stop instead correlates with a logged E301 event, follow the circuit breaker trip resolution for this product instead.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the stop-reason code recorded in Polaris for the affected session, and confirm whether other guns were drawing power at the same moment.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate to the installation/sizing team if reallocation-related stops recur frequently enough to be operationally disruptive.
properties.tags: session stop, modular power sharing, DX-240, DX-360

properties.title: Ethernet Connectivity Failure (E204) on DX-60
properties.problemStatement: A DX-60 unit loses its Ethernet link and logs E204 after the upstream network switch is rebooted or a DHCP lease renewal fails, and does not recover the link on its own.
properties.symptoms: The unit shows Offline in Polaris; the local display may show a network-fault indicator. The condition persists even after the switch and DHCP service are confirmed back online, and does not clear without a manual power cycle of the unit.
properties.environment: DX-60, any firmware; typically a retail or hotel site behind a small, infrequently-managed network switch.
properties.possibleCauses: The DX-60's network stack does not retry DHCP discovery on a backoff schedule after an initial lease-renewal failure; instead it enters a fault state and does not attempt to reacquire an address until the interface is reset. See KI-DX60-001.
properties.resolution: Power-cycle the unit to restore connectivity in the near term. Where the site's network allows it, configure a static IP address for the DX-60 instead of DHCP -- this removes the lease-renewal dependency entirely and is the recommended configuration for a site with a small, infrequently-managed switch. For sites that must remain on DHCP, set the switch port serving the DX-60 to a longer lease time (24 hours or more) and advise site staff to power-cycle the unit after any planned switch maintenance or network firmware update. No permanent unit-side fix has shipped yet for this product.
properties.verificationSteps: After a power cycle, confirm the unit returns to Online in Polaris and re-acquires a valid IP address. If switched to a static IP, confirm no further E204 events over the following 30 days.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if the unit does not recover connectivity after a full power cycle with a confirmed-healthy upstream network.
properties.tags: E204, Ethernet, DHCP, DX-60

properties.title: 4G Connection Failure (E607) on NX-200 With Optional 4G Add-On
properties.problemStatement: An NX-200 unit fitted with the optional 4G add-on module logs E607 and shows as Offline in Polaris, with no accompanying Ethernet or Wi-Fi fault since 4G is typically used as the primary or sole connectivity option on these installs.
properties.symptoms: The unit's display may show a cellular-signal indicator dropping to zero bars before the disconnect. Signal strength at the site is a strong predictor: sites at the edge of carrier coverage or in structures with heavy signal attenuation (e.g. underground or structural parking) see this far more often.
properties.environment: NX-200 with the optional 4G add-on module; any firmware.
properties.possibleCauses: Weak or intermittent carrier signal at the installation site; a SIM/carrier-side provisioning or billing lapse on the cellular data plan; or, less commonly, a modem module fault on the add-on itself.
properties.resolution: First confirm the cellular data plan associated with the unit's SIM is active and in good standing -- a surprising share of 4G connectivity tickets trace back to a lapsed carrier plan rather than a technical fault. If the plan is active, check signal strength at the mounting location; where feasible, relocating the antenna or the unit itself even a short distance can materially improve reception in marginal-coverage locations. For a site with consistently poor coverage, evaluate whether Ethernet is available as a more reliable alternative, since the 4G add-on is intended as a convenience option rather than a guaranteed-coverage connectivity method.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm signal strength reported by the unit improves after any antenna/placement change, and confirm the unit returns to Online in Polaris.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate for a modem-module inspection if the carrier plan is confirmed active and signal strength is confirmed adequate but the unit still cannot maintain a connection.
properties.tags: E607, 4G, cellular, NX-200

properties.title: 4G Modem Connection Failure (E607) on DX-360
properties.problemStatement: A DX-360 unit relying on 4G as its primary connectivity intermittently loses its cellular connection and logs E607, most noticeable during periods of high ambient temperature inside the unit's electronics enclosure.
properties.symptoms: The unit drops to Offline in Polaris and the modem does not always re-register automatically, sometimes taking several minutes to reconnect on its own. Sites relying on 4G as a backup to Ethernet see no visible impact, since the unit fails over automatically.
properties.environment: DX-360, hardware revision B specifically; correlates with high internal enclosure temperature.
properties.possibleCauses: Hardware revision B uses a modem module more sensitive to thermal throttling than the module used from hardware revision C onward. Above roughly 55C internal enclosure temperature, the modem can drop its cellular registration. See KI-DX360-002.
properties.resolution: For hardware-revision-B units relying primarily on 4G, confirm the unit's enclosure ventilation is not obstructed (debris, direct sun exposure without shading, nearby heat sources) and address any obstruction first. Where feasible, run a temporary Ethernet connection as backup connectivity -- the unit fails over to Ethernet automatically if the 4G link drops, eliminating the visible impact even though the underlying thermal sensitivity remains. Hardware revision C and later do not exhibit this symptom; sites with frequent E607 on a hardware-revision-B unit in a hot or poorly ventilated location may request a field modem-module replacement kit through support.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the unit's hardware revision (check the unit label or Polaris device details). After a ventilation fix or modem-module replacement, confirm no further E607 events over a period of elevated ambient temperature.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate to request a modem-module replacement kit for a hardware-revision-B unit with recurring E607 at a confirmed well-ventilated site.
properties.tags: E607, 4G modem, DX-360, hardware revision B, thermal

properties.title: [Superseded] Diagnosing OCPP Connection Issues via Manual Unit Log Pull
properties.problemStatement: This article describes the manual procedure historically used to diagnose OCPP connection issues on NX-400/NX-450 units beyond the specific E217 defect (see KB-NX400-014), by pulling the unit's raw connection log over a local service port.
properties.symptoms: An OCPP disconnect, repeated reconnect loop, or failure to receive remote commands, with no obviously matching error code such as E217, E204, or E607 already covered by a dedicated article.
properties.environment: NX-400 or NX-450, any firmware; historical procedure, superseded on units running Polaris 2024.3 or later.
properties.possibleCauses: A wide range of transient network, backend, or OCPP-protocol-level causes that the manual log pull was used to narrow down case by case, since no automated capture tool existed at the time this procedure was written.
properties.resolution: This manual local-service-port log pull procedure is superseded. Since Polaris 2024.3 added the Remote Diagnostics module, the same OCPP connection log can be captured remotely and automatically from Polaris Device Management without requiring a technician on site with a service laptop -- use the Remote Diagnostics capture instead of this manual procedure for any unit already on Polaris 2024.3 or later. This article is retained only for sites that have not yet been migrated onto a Polaris instance with Remote Diagnostics available.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the site's Polaris instance version before choosing a procedure: 2024.3 or later means Remote Diagnostics should be used instead of this article.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate to confirm Polaris instance version if unsure which procedure applies to a given site.
properties.tags: OCPP, diagnostics, superseded, Remote Diagnostics, NX-400

properties.title: OCPP 2.0.1 Session Resume Failures on NX-450 (Plug & Charge)
properties.problemStatement: An NX-450 unit occasionally fails to resume an OCPP 2.0.1 session correctly after a brief backend connectivity interruption, most noticeable on Plug & Charge sessions where the vehicle's certificate-based authentication must be re-validated on resume.
properties.symptoms: After a short backend interruption (a few seconds to a minute), the session either fails to resume automatically and the vehicle stops charging, or resumes but Polaris briefly shows an authentication-pending state even though charging has already restarted locally.
properties.environment: NX-450, firmware 1.0 specifically; Plug & Charge sessions.
properties.possibleCauses: Firmware 1.0's initial Plug & Charge implementation had a certificate-renewal timing gap during session resume that could cause the resumed session to briefly appear unauthenticated to Polaris even though the vehicle's certificate was still valid.
properties.resolution: Upgrade the unit to firmware 1.1 (released 2026-05), which specifically fixes the Plug & Charge certificate-renewal issue during session resume. Units already on 1.1 or later do not require any workaround. For units still on 1.0, advise drivers experiencing this symptom to briefly unplug and replug if a resumed session does not restart charging within about a minute, which forces a fresh certificate exchange rather than relying on the resume path.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the unit's firmware version. After upgrading to 1.1, confirm a session that experiences a brief backend interruption resumes charging without manual unplug/replug.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if the resume failure recurs on a unit already confirmed running firmware 1.1.
properties.tags: OCPP, Plug and Charge, session resume, NX-450, firmware 1.1

properties.title: Meter Synchronization / Billing Session Mismatch (E404) -- General Diagnostic Guide
properties.problemStatement: A charging session logs E404 in Polaris, indicating the metered energy reading used for billing does not reconcile with the session's raw meter telemetry, and the session is flagged for manual billing review rather than auto-invoiced.
properties.symptoms: The session appears normally in the charger's own history (correct duration, correct energy delivered as reported locally), but the corresponding Polaris invoice line is missing, held for review, or shows an amount inconsistent with the session's own meter delta.
properties.environment: Any Polaris-connected unit; most commonly reported around a mid-session tariff change or an API Management integration's OAuth2 token refresh.
properties.possibleCauses: A clock-skew tolerance in the session-segmentation logic capturing the meter snapshot a few seconds before or after an actual tariff-boundary change (see KI-POLARIS-003); a stale meter-reading cache served to a third-party API integration during an OAuth2 token refresh (see KI-POLARIS-007, fixed in Polaris 2025.4); or, less commonly, a genuine meter communication fault on the unit itself.
properties.resolution: Reconcile the flagged session against the unit's own raw meter-reading log, which is not affected by either known cache/segmentation issue -- only the automated invoice calculation is impacted, not the underlying session or meter data. For a mid-session tariff-change mismatch, review the flagged-for-review billing queue daily rather than assuming all such sessions auto-invoice correctly until the root cause in KI-POLARIS-003 is resolved. For an API-integration mismatch during OAuth2 token refresh, confirm the site's Polaris instance is on 2025.4 or later, which eliminates the stale-reading window entirely; integrations on an earlier version should de-duplicate polls by session ID and prefer the later-timestamped reading.
properties.verificationSteps: Compare the invoiced amount against the raw meter-reading log for the session in question. Confirm the Polaris instance version if the mismatch involves an API integration.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate to the Billing module team for any mismatch that does not correspond to a mid-session tariff change or an OAuth2 refresh window.
properties.tags: E404, meter sync, billing, Polaris

properties.title: Dynamic Load-Balancing Conflict (E315) Between Adjacent NX-400 Units
properties.problemStatement: A pair of NX-400 units sharing the same circuit budget under Polaris dynamic load balancing both throttle to minimum output simultaneously and log E315, instead of negotiating a split of available current.
properties.symptoms: Both units in the pair drop to minimum charging rate at once, typically when both start a session within the same 2-minute window; charging continues at the reduced rate rather than stopping outright.
properties.environment: NX-400 pairs sharing a circuit budget, firmware 4.6 through 4.8.
properties.possibleCauses: A suspected race condition in the load-balancing negotiation handshake when two units request a circuit-budget allocation within the same polling interval (default 5 seconds); the arbitration logic occasionally grants both units a defensive "yield" response instead of exactly one. This is an open investigation -- see KI-NX400-007 for current status.
properties.resolution: No confirmed fix is available yet. As an interim measure, where operationally possible, stagger session starts on shared-circuit unit pairs by at least 3 minutes, which reduces but does not eliminate the reported frequency. This is not resolved by firmware 4.8.1, which is scoped only to the unrelated E217 fix. Do not attempt to work around this by disabling dynamic load balancing entirely unless the site's electrical design has been confirmed to tolerate both units drawing full power simultaneously.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm whether the affected sessions started within the same 2-minute window before logging a new occurrence against the open investigation.
properties.escalationCriteria: Log every new occurrence against KI-NX400-007 with exact session start timestamps for both units, since field reports are the primary evidence source for this open investigation.
properties.tags: E315, load balancing, NX-400, race condition

properties.title: Load-Balancing Conflict (E315) on NX-450 During Plug & Charge Sessions
properties.problemStatement: On NX-450 pairs under dynamic load balancing, a session initiated via Plug & Charge occasionally causes the paired unit to log E315 even though only one of the two units is actually drawing current.
properties.symptoms: The paired unit throttles or reports a load-balancing conflict despite no genuine contention for the shared circuit budget; occurs specifically with mixed Plug & Charge and RFID sessions on the same load-balanced pair.
properties.environment: NX-450 pairs under dynamic load balancing, firmware 1.0 or 1.1.
properties.possibleCauses: The Plug & Charge authentication path bypasses the session-registration call an RFID-initiated session uses to announce itself to the load-balancing arbiter; Plug & Charge registers slightly later, and if the paired unit polls the arbiter in that narrow window it sees only itself as active and incorrectly infers a conflict. See KI-NX450-002.
properties.resolution: For sites running mixed Plug & Charge and RFID sessions on load-balanced NX-450 pairs, increase the arbiter polling interval from the default 5 seconds to 10 seconds in the site's Polaris load-balancing configuration; this gives the Plug & Charge registration call enough time to complete before the next poll and has eliminated the false E315 in field testing at pilot sites. A permanent fix aligning the Plug & Charge registration call with the RFID-session path is planned for a future firmware release; it is not included in release 1.2, which is scoped to energy-metering accuracy only.
properties.verificationSteps: After adjusting the polling interval, confirm no further false E315 events on mixed Plug & Charge / RFID sessions over a 2-week observation window.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if the false conflict persists after the polling-interval adjustment.
properties.tags: E315, NX-450, Plug and Charge, load balancing

properties.title: Nuisance Overcurrent Trips (E301) on DX-120 Units in France
properties.problemStatement: DX-120 installations in France log E301 (overcurrent protection trip) disproportionately often during the first few minutes of a high-power session, even on sites where the incoming ~175A three-phase 400V supply has been verified to meet the published installation requirement with margin.
properties.symptoms: The unit trips and stops delivering power almost immediately after ramp-up begins; the session must be manually restarted, and the trip can recur on the next high-power session start.
properties.environment: DX-120, France installations specifically; any firmware version.
properties.possibleCauses: The DX-120's overcurrent protection threshold is calibrated against a nominal 50Hz supply with limited tolerance for the brief voltage/frequency transients more common on parts of the French low-voltage distribution grid during ramp-up of a high-power DC session, causing the protection logic to trip on a transient rather than a genuine overcurrent condition. See KI-DX120-002; this is an open investigation.
properties.resolution: Reduce the unit's ramp-up rate limit from the default (0 to full power in under 5 seconds) to a slower profile (full power over 15 seconds) in the unit's local power-management configuration. This has eliminated nuisance trips at pilot sites without a measurable impact on typical session charge times. No permanent calibration fix has shipped yet; engineering is gathering grid-side transient data before finalizing a change.
properties.verificationSteps: After adjusting the ramp-up profile, confirm no further E301 trips over a 2-week window of normal high-power session activity.
properties.escalationCriteria: Log every occurrence against KI-DX120-002 with the site's own grid-monitoring data where available, since this evidence is what the ongoing investigation needs.
properties.tags: E301, DX-120, France, overcurrent, grid transient

properties.title: Overcurrent Protection Miscalibration (E301) on DX-240 Under German Grid Compliance Settings
properties.problemStatement: German DX-240 installations configured to the VDE-AR-N 4105 grid-compliance profile logged E301 significantly more often than the same configuration elsewhere, particularly on the 2x120kW configuration under simultaneous dual-gun sessions.
properties.symptoms: The trip could occur mid-session on an established, previously stable charge, not only during initial ramp-up, and correlated with both modular 120kW stages being active at once.
properties.environment: DX-240 in Germany, VDE-AR-N 4105 compliance profile; units on firmware prior to the overcurrent calibration update.
properties.possibleCauses: The VDE-AR-N 4105 compliance profile applies a stricter reactive-power and ramp-rate constraint than the default profile, and the DX-240's overcurrent protection threshold calculation did not correctly account for the additional headroom this constraint consumes when both modular stages are active, causing protection to trip within the unit's genuine safe operating range. See KI-DX240-001, now fixed.
properties.resolution: Confirm the unit has received the overcurrent calibration update, which correctly incorporates the VDE-AR-N 4105 headroom into the threshold calculation for dual-stage operation; this has resolved the issue at all German pilot sites with no recurrence under normal operation. For a unit not yet updated, stagger dual-gun session starts by at least 60 seconds and avoid both guns ramping to full power within the same 10-second window as an interim measure.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the unit's firmware/calibration status. After the update, confirm dual-gun sessions no longer trip E301 under normal simultaneous operation.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if E301 recurs on a unit already confirmed to have received the overcurrent calibration update.
properties.tags: E301, DX-240, Germany, VDE-AR-N 4105, overcurrent

properties.title: Circuit Breaker Trips (E301) on DX-360 High-Current Installations
properties.problemStatement: A DX-360 installation logs E301 during periods of high simultaneous demand across its modular 3x120kW stages, most commonly at logistics-hub or highway sites drawing near the unit's full rated capacity.
properties.symptoms: One or more guns trip and stop delivering power, typically when several guns ramp toward full power within a short window of each other; the unit's own display and Polaris both log the trip with a timestamp and affected gun.
properties.environment: DX-360, needs a dedicated MV/LV substation above ~400A; most often reported at sites near peak simultaneous utilization.
properties.possibleCauses: An undersized or marginally-sized upstream supply relative to genuine peak simultaneous demand across all active guns, rather than a unit defect; less commonly, a site-side protective device miscoordinated with the unit's own overcurrent thresholds.
properties.resolution: Confirm the site's incoming supply was sized and verified against the DX-360's published installation requirement (dedicated MV/LV substation above ~400A) at the time of installation, and against current, not originally-planned, simultaneous gun utilization -- a site that has added guns or increased typical concurrent usage since commissioning may have outgrown its original sizing. If the supply is confirmed adequate, review coordination between the unit's overcurrent protection and any site-side breaker or protective relay for a mismatch in trip curves, which requires an electrical engineer familiar with the site's one-line diagram.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the trip timestamp against Polaris's record of how many guns were active simultaneously at that moment, and compare against the site's rated supply capacity.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate to the installation/electrical engineering team for any suspected supply-sizing or protective-device-coordination issue.
properties.tags: E301, DX-360, overcurrent, supply sizing

properties.title: Slow Charging on NX-400 Dual-Socket Units
properties.problemStatement: A vehicle on an NX-400 unit charges at a materially lower rate than expected given the vehicle's own onboard charger capability and the unit's rated 22kW-per-socket output.
properties.symptoms: Polaris and the unit's own display report a lower current/power delivery than the session's negotiated maximum, without any error code being logged; the session otherwise runs normally start to finish.
properties.environment: NX-400, both sockets in use or a single socket in use; any firmware.
properties.possibleCauses: Dynamic load balancing sharing the site's available circuit budget with another active session on the paired socket or elsewhere on the same circuit, which is expected behavior rather than a fault; the vehicle's own onboard charger being the limiting factor rather than the unit; or a degraded upstream supply voltage at the site reducing effective delivered power.
properties.resolution: First confirm whether another session is active on the paired socket or shared circuit at the same time -- if so, the reduced rate is expected dynamic load-balancing behavior, not a fault, and full-rate charging should resume once the other session ends. If no other session is competing for the circuit budget, confirm the vehicle's own maximum onboard AC charging rate, since many vehicles are limited well below 22kW regardless of what the unit can supply. If neither explains the shortfall, measure the site's supply voltage under load, since a sagging voltage at high demand can reduce delivered power even when the unit itself is functioning correctly.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the delivered power rate with no other session active on the shared circuit, and compare against the vehicle's documented maximum onboard charging rate.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate for a site electrical inspection if reduced delivery persists with no competing session and a vehicle confirmed capable of the full rate.
properties.tags: slow charging, NX-400, load balancing, onboard charger

properties.title: Slow Charging on Nova DC (DX-120 / DX-240) Fast Chargers
properties.problemStatement: A DC fast-charge session on a DX-120 or DX-240 unit delivers power well below the unit's rated output for a materially longer portion of the session than expected.
properties.symptoms: The session's power curve stays flat at a reduced level rather than following the typical DC fast-charge taper (high initial power, gradually reducing as the battery fills); no error code is logged.
properties.environment: DX-120 or DX-240, any firmware; particularly noticeable on a DX-240 with several guns concurrently active.
properties.possibleCauses: On DX-240, modular power-stage sharing across concurrently active guns, which is expected behavior under simultaneous demand rather than a fault; the vehicle's own battery management system limiting charge rate due to battery temperature or state of charge; or a degraded CCS2 connector/cable contact resistance causing the unit to de-rate for thermal safety.
properties.resolution: On a DX-240, confirm whether other guns are concurrently active and drawing from shared modular stages -- if so, the reduced rate reflects normal power sharing across guns, not a fault. If a single gun in isolation is slow, check the vehicle's own charging curve for known temperature- or state-of-charge-related tapering, which is normal EV battery behavior and not specific to this charger. If neither explains the shortfall, inspect the CCS2 connector and cable for wear or contamination, since the unit intentionally reduces power output if it detects elevated contact resistance to protect against overheating at the connector.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm gun-concurrency at the time of the slow session, and inspect the connector visually for wear if concurrency and vehicle-side tapering are both ruled out.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate for a connector/cable replacement if visible wear or contamination is found, or for further investigation if none of the listed causes explains the shortfall.
properties.tags: slow charging, DC fast charging, DX-120, DX-240, connector wear

properties.title: Remote Reboot Failure via Polaris Device Management
properties.problemStatement: A remote reboot command issued from Polaris Device Management for a Nova AC or DC unit does not take effect -- the unit's status does not change and no reboot is observed on site.
properties.symptoms: Polaris shows the reboot command as sent (or, on some releases, as failed/timed out), but the unit's uptime counter does not reset and its display shows no interruption.
properties.environment: Any Polaris-connected Nova AC/DC unit; the command depends on the unit having an active OCPP/backend connection at the time it is issued.
properties.possibleCauses: The unit is actually Offline at the moment the command is issued, so it never receives the command even though the Polaris UI may not make this obviously clear; the unit is mid-session and configured to defer a remote reboot until the session ends, which is expected behavior rather than a failure; or a genuinely stuck OCPP client on the unit that is not processing incoming commands even though it appears Online.
properties.resolution: First confirm the unit's actual connectivity status and heartbeat timestamp at the moment the reboot was issued -- a command sent to an Offline unit will never be delivered and should not be treated as a reboot-command defect. If the unit was genuinely Online and mid-session, confirm whether the session has since ended and retry the reboot command, since some configurations intentionally defer disruptive commands during an active session. If the unit is Online, not mid-session, and still does not respond to a remote reboot, the OCPP client itself is likely stuck and a physical power cycle at the site is required.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the unit's connectivity status and any active session at the time the reboot was issued before escalating a suspected command-delivery defect.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if a unit confirmed Online with no active session repeatedly fails to respond to remote reboot commands, requiring a physical power cycle every time.
properties.tags: remote reboot, Polaris Device Management, stuck OCPP client

properties.title: [Superseded] Recovering an NX-400 From a Failed USB Firmware Update
properties.problemStatement: This article describes the USB-based recovery procedure historically used to restore an NX-400 unit after a firmware update failed to complete or a checksum mismatch left the unit in a non-booting state.
properties.symptoms: The unit's display remains blank or shows a recovery-mode indicator after a firmware update was interrupted (power loss, USB drive removed early) or the update logged E512 and did not complete.
properties.environment: NX-400, any firmware; historical procedure based on the PROC-MAINT-NX400-FWUSB maintenance procedure.
properties.possibleCauses: An interrupted firmware transfer or a checksum mismatch during a local, technician-driven USB firmware update, which was the only supported update method at the time this procedure was written.
properties.resolution: This procedure is superseded. Recovering a unit from a failed firmware update no longer requires an on-site technician with a prepared USB drive following PROC-MAINT-NX400-FWUSB; the current supported method is remote recovery via Polaris Charge Cloud, following PROC-MAINT-NX400-FWREMOTE and KB-NX400-021. Use this article's USB-based steps only for a unit that cannot establish any backend connectivity at all, since the remote recovery path requires the unit to reach Polaris.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the unit has no backend connectivity at all before falling back to this superseded USB procedure; otherwise use the current remote recovery article.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if a unit needs USB-based recovery and PROC-MAINT-NX400-FWUSB itself is unavailable or out of date.
properties.tags: E512, firmware recovery, USB, superseded, NX-400

properties.title: Recovering an NX-400 From a Failed Firmware Update via Polaris Remote Recovery
properties.problemStatement: An NX-400 firmware update fails to complete, logging E512 (interrupted transfer or checksum mismatch), and the unit needs to be restored to a working firmware state without an on-site USB-based recovery.
properties.symptoms: The unit's display shows an update-failed or recovery-mode indicator; the unit remains reachable in Polaris in most cases, since the failure is in the firmware transfer/apply step rather than a loss of backend connectivity.
properties.environment: NX-400, any firmware; unit must retain backend connectivity to Polaris for this procedure to apply.
properties.possibleCauses: An interrupted firmware package transfer (backend connectivity drop mid-transfer) or a checksum mismatch on the downloaded package, most commonly caused by a marginal network connection at the site during the update window.
properties.resolution: This is the current supported recovery method, replacing the older USB-based procedure (KB-NX400-020, superseded). From Polaris Charge Cloud Device Management, trigger a remote firmware recovery for the affected unit, which re-pushes the firmware package and re-validates its checksum before applying, without requiring a technician on site. Follow PROC-MAINT-NX400-FWREMOTE for the full step-by-step procedure. If the site's network connection is unstable enough to have caused the original failure, confirm connectivity is stable before retrying, since a second interrupted transfer will reproduce the same failure.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the unit reports the expected firmware version in Polaris after the remote recovery completes, and confirm the unit resumes normal session activity.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate to the USB-based recovery procedure (KB-NX400-020) only if the unit cannot establish any backend connectivity for remote recovery.
properties.tags: E512, firmware recovery, Polaris Remote Diagnostics, NX-400

properties.title: [Archived] Firmware Update Failure (E512) on Early NX-200 Units
properties.problemStatement: This article documents an early NX-200 firmware updater defect in which an update could log E512 (checksum mismatch) even when the downloaded package was intact, caused by a bug in the updater's own checksum computation rather than the transfer itself.
properties.symptoms: The update process reported a checksum mismatch and rolled back to the prior firmware version, even on units with a stable network connection and a verified-intact download.
properties.environment: NX-200, early production firmware updater versions only; not present on current NX-200 units.
properties.possibleCauses: A bug in the firmware updater's own checksum computation routine produced an incorrect checksum for certain package sizes, causing a false mismatch against the correct, server-side checksum.
properties.resolution: This defect was fixed in a subsequent firmware updater revision; current NX-200 units in the field are on updater versions well past this fix and do not exhibit the symptom. This article is retained for historical reference only and does not reflect a troubleshooting path applicable to any unit currently in service. Do not use this as current guidance for an E512 event on a present-day unit; see the general firmware recovery guidance for the affected product line instead.
properties.verificationSteps: Not applicable -- retained for historical reference only.
properties.escalationCriteria: Not applicable to current units; if a present-day NX-200 logs E512, treat it as a genuine transfer/checksum issue rather than this historical updater bug.
properties.tags: E512, NX-200, archived, updater defect, historical

properties.title: Plug Locking Failure on DX-60
properties.problemStatement: The CCS2 connector on a DX-60 unit fails to lock after being inserted, preventing the session from starting even though the vehicle and unit both otherwise detect a valid plug-in event.
properties.symptoms: The unit's display shows a plug-detected but not-locked state, or the session repeatedly attempts to start and aborts; the connector may feel loose or only partially seated when checked physically.
properties.environment: DX-60, any firmware.
properties.possibleCauses: Debris or moisture in the vehicle's charge inlet or the connector itself preventing full seating; a worn or misaligned locking mechanism on the connector after extended use; or a genuine actuator fault in the unit's connector-locking hardware.
properties.resolution: Inspect and clean both the vehicle's charge inlet and the connector for debris or moisture, and confirm the connector is fully seated (not just resting against the inlet) before assuming a hardware fault. If cleaning and reseating does not resolve it, try the same connector on a different vehicle at the site to isolate whether the fault is vehicle-side or unit-side. A locking failure that reproduces across multiple vehicles on the same connector indicates a worn or faulty locking actuator requiring a technician visit for connector/cable assembly replacement.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the connector locks successfully on a different vehicle before dispatching a technician for a suspected unit-side actuator fault.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate for a connector/cable assembly replacement if the locking failure reproduces across multiple vehicles.
properties.tags: plug locking, CCS2 connector, DX-60

properties.title: Plug Locking Failure on NX-400 / NX-450 AC Connector
properties.problemStatement: The Type 2 AC connector on an NX-400 or NX-450 socket fails to lock after insertion, and the session does not start even though the vehicle registers a valid connection attempt.
properties.symptoms: The unit's display shows an unlocked-connector state; on dual-socket units, only one socket is typically affected while the other locks and charges normally, which helps rule out a site-wide power or firmware cause.
properties.environment: NX-400 or NX-450, any firmware; symptom isolated to one socket in the large majority of reports.
properties.possibleCauses: Debris in the connector or the vehicle's charge port; a worn locking pin or solenoid on the affected socket after extended use; or, less commonly, a vehicle whose own charge port latch is not engaging correctly, which can present identically to a unit-side locking fault.
properties.resolution: Inspect the affected socket's connector for debris and confirm full seating. Test a different vehicle on the same socket, and test the same vehicle on the unit's other socket (on a dual-socket unit) to isolate whether the fault is socket-specific, unit-wide, or vehicle-side. A fault that is consistently isolated to one socket across multiple vehicles indicates a worn locking solenoid on that socket and requires a technician visit; a fault that follows one specific vehicle across multiple sockets points to the vehicle's own charge port rather than the unit.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the isolation test result (socket-specific vs. vehicle-specific) before dispatching a technician.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate for a socket locking-solenoid inspection if the fault is confirmed isolated to one socket across multiple vehicles.
properties.tags: plug locking, Type 2 connector, NX-400, NX-450

properties.title: Billing Session Mismatch (E404) After Mid-Session Tariff Change
properties.problemStatement: A session that crosses a tariff boundary (e.g. peak to off-peak) since the mid-session tariff-change support introduced in Polaris 2025.4 logs E404 on the Billing module, with the invoiced amount not matching the sum of the two tariff-segment meter readings.
properties.symptoms: The session is flagged for manual billing review rather than auto-invoiced; the discrepancy is typically small (a few percent of the total session value) rather than a gross mismatch, which is a useful signal for distinguishing this from an unrelated billing defect.
properties.environment: Polaris 2025.4; sessions that cross a configured tariff boundary mid-session.
properties.possibleCauses: A suspected clock-skew tolerance in the session-segmentation logic, where the meter-reading snapshot taken at the tariff-boundary moment is captured a few seconds before or after the actual tariff-change timestamp, producing a small discrepancy between the two segments' totals and the session's overall meter delta. This is an active internal investigation -- see KI-POLARIS-003.
properties.resolution: Sites relying on mid-session tariff changes should review the flagged-for-review billing queue daily rather than assuming all such sessions auto-invoice correctly. Affected sessions can be manually reconciled against the raw meter-reading log, which is unaffected by the discrepancy -- only the automated invoice calculation is impacted. There is no customer-facing workaround beyond this manual-review process until root cause is confirmed and a fix ships.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the flagged session's raw meter-reading log against the two tariff segments before manually approving or correcting the invoice.
properties.escalationCriteria: Log every occurrence against KI-POLARIS-003 with the exact tariff-boundary timestamp and the session's raw meter log, since this is an active investigation.
properties.tags: E404, billing, tariff change, Polaris

properties.title: Missing Charging Sessions in Polaris Dashboard
properties.problemStatement: A charging session that a driver or site operator confirms took place does not appear in the Polaris dashboard's session history for the corresponding unit.
properties.symptoms: The unit's own local session log (where accessible) shows the session, but it is absent from Polaris's session history for that charger, either entirely or for a window of time around the session.
properties.environment: Any Polaris-connected unit; most commonly reported after a period of degraded backend connectivity.
properties.possibleCauses: The unit was Offline (or intermittently connected) during or shortly after the session, and the session record was not yet synced to Polaris when the report was made -- most sessions sync automatically once connectivity is restored, sometimes with a delay; a reporting/filter setting in the dashboard view excluding the session (e.g. a date-range or site filter); or, less commonly, a genuine session-sync failure that requires a backend resync.
properties.resolution: First confirm the unit's connectivity status around the time of the session and check whether it has since reconnected -- if so, allow time for the automatic sync (typically within a few minutes of reconnection) before treating it as missing. Next, verify the dashboard's active date-range and site filters are not inadvertently excluding the session. If the session is confirmed still missing after connectivity is restored and filters are cleared, request a manual session resync from the unit through Polaris Device Management, which re-pulls the unit's local session log.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm the session appears after clearing dashboard filters and, if needed, after a manual resync.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate to the Device Management team if a manual resync does not recover a session that is confirmed to exist in the unit's own local log.
properties.tags: missing sessions, Polaris dashboard, sync

properties.title: Driver Authentication Issues: RFID, Plug & Charge, and Legacy PIN Fallback
properties.problemStatement: A driver cannot authenticate a session by any available method (RFID card, Plug & Charge where supported, or the legacy PIN-code fallback), and needs a general triage path across all three authentication methods.
properties.symptoms: Depending on the method attempted, the driver may see a card-rejected message (E117), a Plug & Charge session that never authenticates, or a PIN entry that is rejected as invalid despite being entered correctly.
properties.environment: NX-200 and other RFID-capable Nova units; PIN-code fallback applies only to units and sites where it was enabled prior to deprecation.
properties.possibleCauses: For RFID, see the dedicated E117 article for this product; for Plug & Charge, an unresolved vehicle-side certificate issue; for the legacy PIN-code fallback specifically, the method itself is deprecated in favor of RFID and Plug & Charge and may be disabled entirely at sites that have completed migration, which presents as a PIN-entry rejection even when the code entered is correct.
properties.resolution: The legacy PIN-code driver-authentication fallback is deprecated. It remains functional at sites that have not yet migrated off it, but is no longer the recommended authentication method and support for it will not be extended further -- direct drivers and site operators toward RFID card issuance or Plug & Charge (where the vehicle supports it) instead of troubleshooting a PIN-entry rejection as if it were a defect. For RFID rejection, follow the dedicated E117 article for the product in question; for a Plug & Charge failure, follow the OCPP session-resume article for the relevant product.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm whether the site still has PIN-code fallback enabled before troubleshooting a PIN rejection as a defect; if disabled, direct the driver to RFID or Plug & Charge.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate if RFID and Plug & Charge are both unavailable to a driver and the site still requires the deprecated PIN fallback to function.
properties.tags: driver authentication, RFID, Plug and Charge, PIN fallback, deprecated

properties.title: [Draft] Troubleshooting API Authentication Errors With Upcoming Polaris SSO-Based Client Credentials
properties.problemStatement: This draft article is being prepared ahead of an upcoming Polaris API Management enhancement that will let integrators authenticate using an organization's existing SSO identity provider in addition to the current OAuth2 client-credentials method, and will cover the new authentication-error scenarios that method introduces.
properties.symptoms: Not yet applicable in production -- this article is being drafted in preparation for the feature's rollout and should not be used for a current OAuth2 client-credentials authentication error, which is covered by the existing API Management troubleshooting guidance instead.
properties.environment: Upcoming Polaris release, not yet generally available; draft based on the feature's design specification.
properties.possibleCauses: Anticipated causes, pending confirmation once the feature is live: SSO identity-provider metadata misconfiguration on the integrator's side, token audience/scope mismatches specific to the SSO exchange path, and clock-skew issues analogous to those already documented for the existing OAuth2 client-credentials flow.
properties.resolution: Do not publish or reference this article as current guidance until the SSO-based client-credentials feature is generally available and this draft has been validated against a real integration. For a current, production API authentication error, use the existing OAuth2 client-credentials troubleshooting guidance and KI-POLARIS-007 instead.
properties.verificationSteps: Not applicable while in draft status.
properties.escalationCriteria: Not applicable while in draft status; route any current-production API authentication issue to existing OAuth2 guidance instead.
properties.tags: API authentication, SSO, OAuth2, draft, Polaris API Management

properties.title: [Confidential] Diagnosing Suspected Authentication Bypass Attempts on Polaris API Management
properties.problemStatement: This internal-only article provides the diagnostic procedure for support and security personnel investigating a suspected unauthorized attempt to bypass normal OAuth2 client-credentials authentication on the Polaris API Management module.
properties.symptoms: Indicators that warrant this procedure include an unusual pattern of authentication failures against a single client identifier from varying source addresses, API calls presenting a token that does not correspond to any currently issued client-credentials grant, or a spike in authentication attempts well outside a client's normal traffic pattern.
properties.environment: Polaris API Management module, any version supporting OAuth2 client-credentials authentication.
properties.possibleCauses: Most such patterns trace back to a benign cause: a misconfigured integration retrying with stale credentials, a client secret that was rotated without updating every downstream consumer, or an automated monitoring tool polling with an expired token. A genuine bypass attempt is uncommon but is treated with the same procedure regardless of likely cause, since the diagnostic steps are identical either way.
properties.resolution: This procedure is restricted to authorized support and security personnel and is not for customer-facing use. Follow the organization's internal security escalation process for confirmed or suspected unauthorized access attempts; do not attempt independent remediation outside that process. General good practice applies regardless of cause: rotate the affected client's credentials, review access logs for the affected client identifier over the relevant window, and confirm the legitimate integration's downstream systems are updated with any rotated secret before considering the incident closed. This article intentionally omits any specific bypass technique or exploit detail; it documents investigative process only.
properties.verificationSteps: Confirm credential rotation has propagated to all legitimate downstream consumers, and confirm the anomalous authentication pattern has stopped following rotation.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate immediately to the internal security team for any pattern consistent with a genuine, active unauthorized access attempt rather than a benign misconfiguration.
properties.tags: security, authentication, API Management, internal, Polaris

properties.title: Incorrect Energy Readings on NX-400 / NX-450
properties.problemStatement: The energy delivered reported by an NX-400 or NX-450 unit for a session does not match the energy the driver's vehicle reports having received, beyond the small variance normally expected between two independent measurement points.
properties.symptoms: The discrepancy is usually a consistent percentage across sessions on the same unit (suggesting a calibration offset) rather than a one-off anomaly on a single session.
properties.environment: NX-400 or NX-450, any firmware.
properties.possibleCauses: A genuine metering calibration drift on the unit, which can occur gradually over the meter's service life; a difference in measurement point between the unit's meter (AC side, before the vehicle's own onboard charger losses) and the vehicle's reported battery-side energy, which is expected and not a defect since AC-side and battery-side readings are not the same measurement; or, on NX-450 specifically, a unit still on firmware prior to 1.2, which included an energy-metering accuracy improvement.
properties.resolution: First rule out the expected AC-side-vs-battery-side measurement difference, which typically accounts for a small, consistent gap due to onboard-charger conversion losses and is not something the unit can or should correct for. For an NX-450 on firmware prior to 1.2, upgrade to 1.2 or later, which improves metering accuracy. If a consistent, larger-than-expected offset remains after ruling out both of those, request a field metering calibration check, since a drifted meter requires physical recalibration or replacement rather than a configuration change.
properties.verificationSteps: Compare the reported energy against a known-reference measurement (e.g. a calibrated external meter) rather than only against the vehicle's own reported figure, which is not itself independently calibrated against the unit.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate for a field metering calibration check if a consistent offset remains after ruling out measurement-point differences and, on NX-450, confirming firmware 1.2 or later.
properties.tags: energy readings, metering, NX-400, NX-450, calibration

properties.title: Incorrect Energy Readings on DX-120 in France (Grid Frequency Variation)
properties.problemStatement: DX-120 installations in France occasionally report an energy reading with a small but measurable positive bias compared to a calibrated reference meter, more often than the same unit configuration in other served markets.
properties.symptoms: The bias is small (typically low single-digit percent) but consistent across sessions at affected sites, and is not accompanied by any error code.
properties.environment: DX-120, France installations; correlates with periods of grid-frequency variation on parts of the French low-voltage distribution grid.
properties.possibleCauses: The unit's metering calculation assumes a tightly stable 50Hz grid frequency; on parts of the French low-voltage distribution grid where frequency varies slightly more than the meter's assumed tolerance, the energy integration calculation can accumulate a small systematic bias over a session, distinct from the separate overcurrent-protection grid transient issue affecting DX-120 in France (KI-DX120-002), which is unrelated to metering.
properties.resolution: This is a known, low-magnitude local grid characteristic rather than a unit defect, and does not currently have a firmware-level correction shipped for this specific market. For a site where the bias affects billing reconciliation beyond an acceptable tolerance, request a field metering calibration check, which can adjust for the local site's typical grid-frequency profile. Do not conflate this with the DX-120 overcurrent nuisance-trip issue in France (KB-DX120-002) -- the two are unrelated despite both being France-specific grid characteristics on the same product.
properties.verificationSteps: Compare the unit's reported energy against a calibrated reference meter over several sessions to confirm a consistent bias before requesting a calibration check.
properties.escalationCriteria: Escalate for a field metering calibration check if the confirmed bias exceeds the site's billing reconciliation tolerance.
properties.tags: energy readings, metering, DX-120, France, grid frequency
